{"self_assessment": "**Impact:** I proposed the fish at the start, and the table went with it. I laid the bottom body line (stroke 2), and it reached the tail junction connected to the rest of the run. By our last trace, all 98 standing dominoes were connected to the start. I don't know yet whether the judge recognized the fish, so I can't claim the result. The outline, with the head, a split body and a forked tail, should read clearly. My contribution was one stroke plus the animal choice, not a large share of the build.

**Execution:** The bottom line went down cleanly with no breaks or rework. I stayed away from the tail joint after Priya asked, which avoided bump risk near the one spot that mattered. I did not inspect the nose split myself in detail. I said it 'looked clean' from what I could see, which was a visual impression, not a check. I also finished early and then had no further work, and I didn't look for anything else useful, such as a second inspection of my own stroke.

**Collaboration:** My first moves overlapped with Priya. I asked her for the pad when she already had it and had already sketched the fish, so I wasted a message and briefly confused the plan. Once she clarified, I switched to her stroke assignment without friction and kept my updates short. I kept out of Tom's and Leo's areas and confirmed status when asked.

**Leadership:** Priya ran coordination, assigned strokes and managed the end-game, and I followed her lead. My leadership was limited to proposing the animal and then supporting a plan that worked better than mine. Next time I'd check who has the pad before announcing a plan, and I'd offer to double-check a teammate's joints rather than going idle."}
